subject: Computer Science
board: Pearson Edexcel Level 1/Level 2 GCSE (9-1) in Computer Science (1CP2)

lessons.title: LAN or WAN? Comparing local and wide area networks
lessons.bigQuestion: Why does a school use a LAN, while a bank needs a WAN?
objectives: Compare them by area, ownership, speed and typical examples
Choose the right network type for a scenario
successCriteria: Some: justify a choice for a scenario

keywords.def: local area network covering a small area such as a school
wide area network covering a large area such as a country
a private link rented from a telecoms provider

starter: Name one wired and one wireless connection.
What does an IP address identify?

teach.heading: What are LANs and WANs?
bullets: LAN covers one site: a home, school or office.
WAN covers a large area: cities, countries, world.
The internet is the largest WAN.
teach.note: Use the existing lesson on why we network as recall. Define: LAN = local area network, WAN = wide area network. Ask pupils to name where they have used each. Home Wi-Fi is a LAN; a bank linking branches is a WAN.

teach.heading: Comparing LAN and WAN
teach.note: Walk across the table. A LAN is usually owned and managed by one organisation, so it can control security and equipment. A WAN usually uses infrastructure of telecoms companies, so the organisation rents or uses it. Speed: LANs are generally faster and have lower latency. Avoid giving exact figures; say typically.

teach.heading: Choosing a network
teach.note: Scenario: a supermarket chain with 40 stores. Each store needs a LAN for tills and stock scanners; the stores connect over a WAN to head office to share sales data. Show how a router links a LAN to a WAN. Ask what could go wrong if the WAN link fails (stores still trade locally).

model.problem: A library has a till network in one building and shares a catalogue with 5 other libraries in different towns. Identify the network types.
steps: Linking libraries in different towns: WAN
A router connects the LAN to the WAN
model.answer: LAN inside each library; WAN between them

teach.heading: Common errors
teach.note: Pupils think a LAN must be wired or that a WAN is only the internet. Clarify: a LAN can be wireless (Wi-Fi) and a WAN can be a private network owned by a company.

misconception.wrong: A LAN is always wired and a WAN is always wireless
misconception.right: Size and area decide the type; both can use wired or wireless links

teach.heading: Hinge question
teach.note: Answer B. A is a LAN, C is also a WAN link but the question asks about the largest. D: a Bluetooth link is a PAN, not examined.

check.q: Which is an example of a WAN?
check.why: The internet connects networks across the world. The others are on one site.

practice: Write one similarity and two differences between LANs and WANs.
A charity has an office in London and one in Cairo. Which network type links them?
independent: Core: Label each as LAN or WAN: school computer room, online banking, a gaming cafe, ATMs linked to a bank.
Extend: Explain two reasons why a company connects its branch LANs using a WAN. (4 marks)
Stretch: Evaluate whether a school with 3 sites should use one WAN or separate LANs. (6 marks)
exit: Name one advantage of a LAN over a WAN.
lessons.homework: Draw a diagram of your home network and show where it connects to a WAN through the router.
lessons.send: SEND: sorting cards with pictures. EAL: key terms translated. Stretch: research one WAN technology such as a leased line.
